text:
Max Sasson is a Ranger now. Vancouver traded the undrafted forward to New York this week, a move read in Vancouver as the Canucks opening for business, and the Rangers have said they expect him to make an instant impact. He arrives with six goals and eight points in 26 games, playing about 12 minutes a night in a depth role.

The goals are a bit ahead of his chances (six on 3.5 expected), but the bigger number runs the other way. Vancouver scored 15.4 fewer goals than its chances deserved with Sasson on the ice, one of the largest gaps in the league, and that cost him points. Evolving-Hockey saw the same thing last season, and noted he skated with some of the weakest teammates in the league.

He brings speed (93rd percentile top speed in NHL EDGE tracking) and, per Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking, carries the puck in on 57% of his entries, high for a bottom-six forward. Better linemates in New York could turn his chances into more goals. Watch his minutes and who he lines up with.
headline: Sasson heads to New York owed some goals
